x_q5: I think aging is when the body's various functions begin to decline: having less energy than when young, muscle atrophy, osteoporosis, worsening memory, and so on. Metabolism also becomes slower.
t_q7: Healthcare system & caregiving|Chronic disease & physical health|Mental & emotional health|Social connection & isolation|Quality of life
x_q7: Older adults gradually lose the ability to care for themselves and may not receive adequate care. Younger family members are often not nearby, leading to poorer quality of life. They increasingly struggle to keep up with rapid changes, become mentally isolated from the outside world, and feel physically unable to manage.
x_q8: Convenient, accessible services are very important. Many restaurants and stores no longer accept cash or require ordering by scanning a code, which is inconvenient for older adults. This directly affects their quality of life and should be addressed quickly.
x_q9: In China, communities have convenient canteens, and the government provides meal subsidies for older people by adding money to their senior cards every three months. Neighborhood committees also care about older residents and regularly visit to check on them. I think China is getting better at providing this kind of care.
t_q10: Physical health & mobility|Memory & cognitive sharpness|Appearance
x_q10: Health, memory, and beauty.
x_q11: Maintain a healthy daily routine, do not drink alcohol, and do not smoke.
t_rank: Personal relevance|Broad benefit to society|Access, cost & equity|Healthcare system & caregiving|Chronic disease & physical health|Technology & AI|Prevention & early detection|Reproductive health & fertility|Population & societal burden
x_rank: Widespread access is most important. Even if solutions exist, they are of little use if they are too niche, expensive, or difficult to implement. Ultimately, solutions must be used by people. Personally, I think machine learning and AI can effectively improve medical care, and I am more interested in disease prediction, so I put them second. Reproductive health is not especially important to me personally, but society may value it more as birth rates continue to fall.
t_excite: Chronic disease & physical health|Technology & AI|Research, science & treatments|Prevention & early detection
x_excite: Topic iii: Disease prediction and precision health are very important. Many diseases cannot be treated effectively or their symptoms relieved because they are detected too late. AI and machine learning are developing rapidly, so I am optimistic about this field and hope for major research breakthroughs.
t_concern: Access, cost & equity|Healthcare system & caregiving|Social connection & isolation|Technology & AI|Safety, accuracy & misuse|Research, science & treatments|Prevention & early detection
x_concern: Topic iii: Even if we develop these solutions, clinical trials will probably take considerable time. If the predicted risk is high or the methods are more invasive, I would worry and be unsure whether to undergo testing. I also worry about disclosure of my own and my family's information, and the cost of advanced testing equipment.
t_ethics: Chronic disease & physical health|Technology & AI|Research, science & treatments
x_ethics: Anything involving invasive experiments or surgery requires careful consideration. Gene editing, for example, remains a somewhat sensitive topic in medicine. How can we ensure that information used in machine learning is not leaked, especially rare blood types or rare disease cases?
